title: Multi-Threshold Pass-Count Preservation under Bounded Score Perturbations
abstract: For a finite threshold list, the pass-count $C(x)=\sum_i \mathbf{1}\{x\ge T_i\}$ is invariant under $|x'-x|\le\varepsilon$ whenever every cut is buffered ($x\ge T_i+\varepsilon$ or $x<T_i-\varepsilon$). Lean \texttt{LEAN\_FULL}.
problem: The multi-threshold operator returns the Nat pass-count $C(x;T_\bullet)=|\{i:x\ge T_i\}|$ over a finite list of cuts (equality passes).
stability: Perturbation: $|x'-x|\le\varepsilon$. Hypothesis allCoordsStable: each $T_i$ satisfies $x\ge T_i+\varepsilon$ or $x<T_i-\varepsilon$. Stability: $C(x';T_\bullet)=C(x;T_\bullet)$. Sharpness: if $x$ lies in $[T-\varepsilon,T+\varepsilon)$ for a single cut, some admissible $x'$ changes the count.
definitions:
\begin{definition}[Pass bit / count]
$\mathrm{passBit}(x,T)=1$ if $x\ge T$ else $0$; $C(x;[])=0$ and $C(x;T{::}\mathrm{tail})=\mathrm{passBit}(x,T)+C(x;\mathrm{tail})$.
\end{definition}
\noindent\textbf{Assumptions.} $\varepsilon\ge 0$, $|x'-x|\le\varepsilon$, and allCoordsStable.
intuition: Each buffered cut is a scalar threshold bit; the count is the sum of those bits. If any cut sits in its unstable band, that bit can flip.
consequences: Unordered pass-counts for multiple cuts; constraint conjunction/disjunction reuse buffered bits. Ordered bucket indices are a separate ranking/bucket operator.
